html:
Albania is a small mountainous country on the Adriatic coast of the Balkans. It appears on the map from 1914, two years after it declared independence from the Ottoman Empire.

Albanians speak a language that forms its own branch of the Indo-European family. Their hero is Skanderbeg, who fought the Ottomans in the 1400s. After his death the country stayed Ottoman for over four centuries, and most Albanians became Muslim, while large Catholic and Orthodox minorities remained.

Independence was declared at Vlorë in November 1912, during the Balkan Wars, and the great powers recognised it in 1913, leaving many Albanians outside its borders, above all in Kosovo. The new state was weak and was occupied by several armies in the First World War. Ahmet Zogu took power and crowned himself King Zog in 1928. Mussolini's Italy invaded in 1939.

From 1944 the communist Enver Hoxha ruled until his death in 1985. He broke with Yugoslavia, then with the Soviet Union in 1961, then with China in 1978, and left Albania one of the most closed countries on earth. In 1967 he banned all religion. Communism ended in 1991. A collapse of pyramid savings schemes in 1997 led to riots and near anarchy. Albania joined NATO in 2009, and many Albanians live and work abroad.
sum: Albania is a small mountainous country on the Adriatic coast of the Balkans. It appears on the map from 1914, two years after it declared independence from the Ottoman Empire.
